It maps feed entries to a consistent state space, enabling downstream probabilistic validation. The JEV signal architecture \mathcal{A} then applies a shared-state abstraction over these validated entries, enabling parallel decision heads and confidence-based routing. This structure aligns with GSE’s state-transition logic, where \mathcal{A} defines a deterministic decision kernel. The AlphaCode framework \mathcal{E} extends this by introducing agent-level modularity, allowing for dynamic tool and model selection. Together, these primitives form a layered system where \mathcal{K} validates input, \mathcal{A} structures decision-making, and \mathcal{E} executes actions. Failure modes include \mathcal{K} breakdown due to href mismatches, \mathcal{A} misalignment from inconsistent inputs, and \mathcal{E} instability from tool/model failures.
